title: Blankfein's own AI-bubble / 2008-AAA analogy + the Deaton reply (bailout & self-marked-value thread)
source: Primary: Lloyd Blankfein (@lloydblankfein) post, and John E. Deaton (@JohnEDeaton1) quote-reply, both 2026-08-22 (captured via X syndication). Claims independently verified against Congress.gov/GovTrack (EESA/TARP), ProPublica Bailout Tracker + Treasury (Goldman CPP), SEC 2010-123 (Abacus), and DOJ 2016 RMBS settlement. This block records a TOP-BANKER PRIMARY-SOURCE statement that itself draws the map's core analogy (self-marked AI value <-> AAA mortgage bonds that went to zero), plus a fact-check of the reply's characterizations. Rhetoric ('POS', 'utter garbage') is opinion and is NOT ingested as fact; only the checkable claims are graded.
grade: per-edge in notes (fact | contested | mischaracterization | opinion)

verification.verbatim_blankfein: Risk management 101 - every exposure should have a limit, even when you're sure nothing could go wrong. After all, the Titanic sank and AAA mortgage bonds went to zero. I worry about the market's (and the economy's) unlimited appetite for exposure to the positive AI revenue story.
verification.verbatim_deaton: EVERYONE: Meet Lloyd Blankfein - he's one of the Wall Street Bankers (aka POS) @EdMarkey chose to bailout in 2008. Lloyd was CEO of @GoldmanSachs. His 'risk management 101' back then was packaging toxic mortgage bonds - utter garbage - stamping AAA investment grade on it -

claims.claim: Blankfein was CEO of Goldman Sachs
claims.detail: CEO June 2006 (succeeding Hank Paulson, who left to become Treasury Secretary and later architected TARP) through 2018 (succeeded by David Solomon).

claims.claim: Ed Markey 'chose to bailout' Wall Street in 2008
claims.detail: Markey was a U.S. REPRESENTATIVE (MA-7), not yet a Senator; he publicly maintained support for and voted for the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008 (TARP), which passed the House 263-171 on Oct 3, 2008. 'Chose to bailout' = one of 263 House yes votes on a $700B program, not a personal selection of Goldman.

claims.claim: Goldman Sachs was bailed out in 2008
claims.detail: Goldman received $10B via TARP's Capital Purchase Program on Oct 28, 2008; also drew Fed facilities and a $5B Buffett/Berkshire injection. Repaid the $10B on Jun 9, 2009 with ~$1.4B profit to Treasury (~23% annualized). SIGTARP later noted Goldman 'took $10 billion in TARP bailout funds' while it had misrepresented RMBS quality.

claims.claim: Goldman was 'packaging toxic mortgage bonds - utter garbage'
claims.detail: Goldman underwrote/sold RMBS and synthetic CDOs tied to subprime; DOJ 2016: $5.06B settlement for serious misconduct in RMBS marketing (knew of defective loans). SEC 2010: $550M Abacus settlement - Goldman acknowledged marketing materials were incomplete (omitted that Paulson & Co. helped pick the portfolio and was short it). Note: Goldman did NOT admit fraud in the Abacus settlement.

claims.claim: Goldman was 'stamping AAA investment grade on it'
claims.detail: The AAA ratings were assigned by the NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED RATING AGENCIES (Moody's, S&P, Fitch) - NOT by Goldman. Goldman structured/packaged and sold the securities and arranged them to obtain AAA tranches; the rating stamp itself was the agencies' act. The distinction matters: it is the ratings-capture (Goodhart) leg of the story, and attributing the AAA stamp to Goldman is inaccurate even though Goldman's conduct in selling the paper is well-documented.

claims.claim: Blankfein now warns of the AI 'revenue story' the way AAA bonds went to zero
claims.detail: The quoted post is Blankfein's own risk-limit warning explicitly analogizing the market's 'unlimited appetite' for AI-revenue exposure to AAA mortgage bonds that went to zero - a top-banker primary source echoing this map's self-marked-value / Minsky-fragility thesis.

$10B TARP Capital Purchase Program injection Oct 28 2008; repaid Jun 9 2009 with ~$1.4B profit to Treasury. Enabled by EESA/TARP (House 263-171, Oct 3 2008; Rep. Markey voted yes) (fact).

Moody's/S&P/Fitch assigned the AAA ratings - correcting the reply's claim that Goldman itself 'stamped AAA'. This is the ratings-capture (Goodhart) leg (fact/correction).
